articleTitle: Free Route Airspace-Graphs, Networks, Algorithms
abstract: Free Route Airspace, a new concept of air transport, has been designed to eliminate the negative impact of air traffic on the environment. The primary goal of this contribution was to allocate mathematical models, graphs, and networks to this new concept. Another goal was to show how to work with this object using programs. Data and program analysis were performed in the MATLAB environment. The examined network type allows a two-level optimization approach.

articleTitle: Utilization of NDT methods in aircraft maintenance
abstract: Currently in the world is the most extended and most used mode of transport is transport by airplane. Non-destructive testing of materials plays an important role in the quality management system. Such testing enables the early detection of inside component defects that could affect its effective use. Different already proven methods based on physical principles are used to evaluate and detect cracks by non-destructive testing. The advantage of non-destructive testing over usual testing is that the component remains unchanged in all respects for further use even after the use of any non-destructive method. Techniques, analysis, necessary equipment, experiments, and advantages of individual non-destructive methods are described in the article from a comparative point of view.

articleTitle: Innovations in the field of aircraft ground handling
abstract: The article deals with progressive and innovative methods used in the field of technical aircraft testing. In the introduction, the authors define and introduce the concept of ground handling of the aircraft and also describe its most important components. In the following chapter, the authors deal with virtual reality as the most potent tool in this area and also present its current use in one of the tasks of ground handling. The third chapter presents innovative technical solutions used for various ground handling activities. The conclusion of the article is a summary in which the authors point out further potential directions in this area and the issues that need to be addressed in the future.

articleTitle: Transformation of EUROCONTROL’s classroom courses into remote learning
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic has forced the students, the teachers and all educational institutions to rapidly adapt to the online learning. The EUROCONTROL Institute of Air Navigation Services – EUROCONTROL’s training centre, which supplies more than 200 courses related to ATM/CNS, had to review its traditional training modules to ensure continuous delivery of the courses and in the desired quality. The theoretical courses were relatively easily transformed to virtual courses by using one of the major webinar platforms – Zoom. However, the courses with hands-on sessions were much more difficult to modify. Numerous challenges included cybersecurity of the test equipment to be connected to the internet, the quality of the connection, the adequate number of participants and, naturally, reasonable costs. This article describes the transformation of courses for the 3 EUROCONTROL’s surveillance products ARTAS, SASS-S and SDDS from face-to-face to virtual.

articleTitle: Economic comparison of airlines in Asia-Pacific region based on specific indicators in years 2018-2020
abstract: The influence of Covid-19 still persists in the world. Air traffic recovery is slow. The recovery of air transport is also influenced by the emergence of new variants of Covid-19. The Asia-Pacific region was the first to be directly affected by the Covid-19 pandemic. After a relatively strong drop in air transport in early 2020, the situation in the region has stabilized. The research is focused on the economic parameters of airlines in the Asia-Pacific region. 14 airlines were included in the research. In the evaluation process, the research focused on operating revenue, operating costs and net profit or loss. By comparing the economic indicators of airlines in the years 2018-2020, a comprehensive view of the development of economic indicators before and during the Covid-19 pandemic was created. The research shows that most airlines in the region have experienced high financial losses compared to previous years.

articleTitle: Blowing as a mean of drag reduction of wing – strut junction
abstract: High aspect ratio is well-known mean to reduce induced drag of a wing. The problems with strength and stiffness of a high aspect ratio wing can be suppressed by a strut. A junction between the wing and the strut is a source of interference drag that can be potentially decreased by flow control performed by blowing. Continuous and pulse blowing in the wing – strut junction was studied both experimentally and numerically. The results indicate the influence of the mass flow, frequency and injected momentum on the efficiency of the blowing as a mean of the drag reduction.

articleTitle: General Conceptual Design of Small Unmanned Aircraft Situational Control
abstract: The article focuses on the design and analysis of combined automatic engine and flight control for small unmanned aircraft with fixed wings. According to current trends in UAV control, it has been demonstrated that knowledge of aircraft limits and a system that is correctly set according to the flight envelope is required for proper aircraft control, combining methods for classifying individual flight phases. Each flight phase contains its own flight envelope, which limits the limits of the aircraft. The correct classification indicates a functional flight envelope that is able to warn or intervene in the control at the limit or when the flight envelope is exceeded. The aim of the article is the correct classification of flight phases and created flight situations, which will allow to evaluate the situation and alert the pilot to a change in the position of the aircraft.

articleTitle: Control of the Airplane Sighting System
abstract: The paper analyzes the transformation of the movement of the tracking optoelectric system in a selected phase of flight in the longitudinal plane. Mathematical models of this integrated system are described by transfer functions, which are transferred to the state space with evaluation in the MATLAB/Simulink simulation environment. The control of an automatic tracking system on an aircraft is determined in the direction of the tracking line with its mutual symmetry between two objects. A gyroscope is placed on the tracking system, the function of which is to measure the angular velocities of the tracking line. The output of the tracking optoelectronic system is the angular velocity of the tracking system line control, which is the main input to the prediction computer for calculating the take-off angle and to control the aircraft system to provide a command to increase dynamics in the tilt position control system.

articleTitle: Aerobatic Trainer Aircraft Conceptual Design
abstract: In recent years, we can observe a lack of trainer aircraft suitable for initial and also for advanced aerobatics training. In addition, it should be mentioned that Upset Prevention and Recovery Training provision has been applied, which has increased the demands on the capabilities of trainer aircraft. This paper is devoted to introducing the conceptual design of an aerobatic trainer two-seater aircraft with a tandem arrangement. The introductory part is aimed at a state-of-the-art review of the aerobatic aircraft portfolio. The main section of the paper discusses the design creation of a training aerobatic aircraft in the software Rhinoceros and the determination of technical and operational parameters. Analyses of aerodynamic characteristics precede the conclusion.

articleTitle: Comparison of Three Camera Calibrations Based on UAV Images
abstract: The paper compares three on-site camera calibrations based on the same test area consisting of evenly distributed control points on a slightly moderated terrain having a size of 200x200 m area. The images were taken with three different UAVs and all camera calibrations were calculated with the same software. The goal of the comparative study was to determine the maximum accuracy that could be achieved for the same test area under slightly different conditions.

articleTitle: Transport constructions, their safety in connection with the protection of the population
abstract: The current safety situation and the conclusions of a number of strategic and conceptual materials call for a wider involvement of the system of protection of the population in the field of spatial planning as well as construction management. The aim of the article is to approximate the requirements of population protection for transport structures. The article outlines the approaches of division of buildings in the Czech Republic and Slovakia. An example of building division approaches in the Czech Republic is public infrastructure, which is understood as transport and technical infrastructure, civic amenities and public spaces established and used in the public interest. Slovakia deals with residential and non-residential buildings, civil engineering, and public and technical equipment in the area. After approaching the approaches of division of buildings, the article deals more with transport structures, specifically airports and their division.The other parts of the article describe the link to protection zones, legislation and requirements for airports and requirements for their location. The result of the article is an outline of the requirements for the protection of the population for transport constructions, ie also airports applied in the Czech Republic and Slovakia.

articleTitle: Abrasion of tires in aviation
abstract: Abrasion is a significant issue not only in the automobile industry, but also in the field of aircraft tires.Manufacturers of aviation tires set standards for the amount of wear that can be tolerated. The tire must be replaced or retreaded if these restrictions are exceeded. The tire should be able to resist as many take-off and landing cycles as feasible until then. In pre-flight modeling, abrasion models should aid in predicting wear behavior. The weight loss of the rubber sample is measured at various pressures and sliding speeds to evaluate abrasion. During an unsteady load, tire wear is measured.

articleTitle: Aviation safety in the European transport policy
abstract: The article is an attempt to refer to the prevention of air operations in communication aviation. Overall, the framework set by the European Aviation Safety Agency allows airline managers to set quality standards and flight safety. Aviation and safety go hand in hand: air transport could not develop without strict rules guaranteeing a high level of safety.The purpose of the article is to indicate that an important issue in the prevention of flight safety is the detection and recording of aviation incidents and failure factors, their thorough investigation as well as searching for sources of threats that may, under appropriate conditions, become the cause of an air accident. Since the plane enables fast and long journeys: aviation safety also means advanced and effective international cooperation. The European Union aims to achieve the status of the safest airspace in the world by 2050.

articleTitle: Life cycle assessment of environmental impacts of transport infrastructure for evidence-based policy making
abstract: The topic of environmental protection and elimination of negative impacts is currently highly discussed at regional and global levels. The current goals of Green Transport are focused on reducing the fuel consumption, creating infrastructure solutions, reducing noise, reducing the transport costs, reducing traffic jams and, ultimately, on complying with the legislative restrictions. The main goal of the paper is to create a concept for the assessment of the environmental impacts of transport infrastructure by specifying the areas of assessment for selected types of transport, using the life-cycle method, with a focus on carbon dioxide emissions. To achieve the main objective in the paper authors used a life cycle assessment method that takes into account the entire life cycle of the product used, from extraction of raw materials, through the production of energy and materials, its use and disposal at the end of life to final elimination of the product.

articleTitle: Accuracy of Determining the Position of Flying Objects in the Conditions of Ideal Time Base Synchronization
abstract: The article analyzes the issue of determining the position of flying objects that operate in the aviation communication network. The architecture of the proposed model was verified on the created computer model. The computer simulation was performed in the Matlab software environment. In the article, the parameters found for the accuracy of determining its position based on information from users of the aviation communication network were presented. In this case, the model in terms of ideal time synchronization of time basics of individual users of the aviation communication network was considered.

articleTitle: Proactive Mechanisms against Occurrences in Civil Aviation
abstract: The top priority for every organization within airline industry has always been safety. It is fundamental to the purpose of the reporting of incidents and accidents that the knowledge gained from occurrences investigations are disseminated so that all in the business involved may take a good from them. However, the current aviation safety system is mainly a reactive and prescriptive. This paper brings a brief overview on Regulation (EU) No 376/2014 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 3 April 2014 on the reporting, analysis and follow-up of occurrences in civil aviation, including categories of reportable occurrences as well as other relative legal acts. Notwithstanding, existing legislation requires to conduct the in-depth analyses of all occurrences. In this study Root Cause Analysis is described as an appropriate method for such analysis. The aim of this paper is to give an overview on selected EU legislation acts which are ruling mandatory mechanisms to collect, evaluate, process and store occurrences in civil aviation as well as a method which helps disclose hidden boosters of safety incidents and accidents.

articleTitle: Identification of Research Problems to Create a Digital Content for Selected Flight Training Subjects
abstract: The article presents selected aspects of the research topic, which is aviation education in the era of digitization and internationalization. We can only investigate specific research problems. The main goal of the article is therefore to identify research problems to create a digital content of selected subjects for flight training of future pilots in aviation law, aviation regulations, air navigation and aviation meteorology, within the “Integrated Laboratory for Digital Aviation Education” at the Faculty of Aeronautics of the Technical University in Košice. The authors present a description of the research plan for solving specific research problems within the research topic.

articleTitle: Modern Flight School with Electronic Smart Concept
abstract: This paper focuses on selecting the most suitable smart solution system for the Air Training and Educational Centre at the University of Žilina. The selection was based on answers from a survey about system properties and research, where the preferences of instructors and students during their practical flight training at the University of Zilina were shown. We tried to identify the basic functions and mechanisms of the systems and compared them with the research findings. The basic goals were fulfilled by selecting three systems which met the requirements of students, instructors as well as the flight school. The outline of one of these smart systems would simplify the flight training of students in the future and would increase the overall efficiency of the flight school.

articleTitle: Differences in low-cost airline operating models in 2018, 2019 and 2020 – comparison of easyJet, Ryanair and Wizz Air
abstract: This paper compares the operating models of selected low-cost airlines. Comparative analysis works with available data from the annual reports of easyJet, Ryanair and Wizz Air. Operating models of these airlines are compared based on selected indices using benchmarking comparison. Results of analysis point out that easyJet and Ryanair dominated in 3 out of 8 indices and Wizz Air only in 2 out of 8 indices, in 2018 and 2019. In 2020, when a pandemic broke out, easyJet dominated in 5 indices, Wizz Air in 2 and Ryanair only in 1 index. In the overall three-year evaluation, easyJet achieved the best results, so it can be assumed that its operating model, compared to others, is the best one.

articleTitle: The Overall Cumulative Impact of Covid-19 and Brexit on European Supply Chains
abstract: Supply chains are usually perceived as a stable environment where only local or regionalised disruptions may happen, thus this paper focuses on the unpreceded situation where cumulative impact of Brexit, Covid-19, and Suez Canal blockage on supply chains. Each event has been analysed from different angles to provide a wider view and depiction of complexity of modern supply chains as well as their vulnerability when it comes to cumulative impacts of major disruptions.

articleTitle: Business Continuity Management Through Stakeholders Collaboration and Participation
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic highlights the pursuit of business continuity efforts in a variety of companies that adapt their theoretical plans to the ever-changing environment of today’s society. Business continuity generally increases the resilience of businesses to disruptions, interruptions, or loss of ability to meet their key objectives. Business continuity is therefore important in fulfilling the agreed tasks and outlined strategies. Theoretically, most railway companies have a business continuity plan, however, get hardly ever implemented. The main reason behind that is the fact the railway participation in the transport system, has a very specific role in providing transport services. The continuity of railway activities fulfils a specific task, providing transport services, which is one of the basic functions of the state.The application of participatory continuity can also be used in air transport.

articleTitle: Topology Optimization Study of Airplane Controls Console
abstract: The article presents a study on topology optimization applied on an aluminium alloy airplane controls console to save the weight. The weight is one of the crucial factors of airplane structures affecting their efficiency, payload, performance, and costs. The article introduces to topology optimization as a SW tool to redistribute the part material yet enabling to carry the applied load. First, it is analysed the load acting on the console during airplane flight and ground operations as well. Next, the most crucial load is applied on the console under topology optimization procedure using the SW Ansys Workbench 2020. The differential influence of load cases is considered using the weight function reflecting the load occurrence. The optimized console shape is finally modified using the SW Autodesk Inventor to achieve the stiffness and strength of the origin console. Achieved reduction of the console weight is 11%. The final console shape is possible to produce using conventional or additive technologies. The article gives the recommendations for further development.

articleTitle: Evaluation of operating efficiency of the baggage handling system, depending on the damage of identification labels
abstract: The authors investigated the impact of anti-pandemic measures on the function of the Baggage Handling System (BHS). Disinfection procedures can damage the bag tag (BT) used to identify and sort luggage. Data obtained from a standard literature search were used to construct a 3D simulation in the Tecnomatix Plant Simulation 15 software. The simulation showed that decreasing the success rate of BT automatic scanning produces increasing the need of manual scanning. It can eventually result in the formation of additional bottlenecks, identification problems, and the loss of luggage. This consequently leads to further delays in the handling of luggage (flights). It also considerable increases the possibility of transmission of the corona virus (COVID disease) due to additional human contact, and in addition to increased costs due to the need to expand manual scanning workplaces. Considering all factors, it is recommended to look for suitable disinfection methods with no damage to the BT along with other BHS components.

articleTitle: Covid 19 and its impact on AMDAR data
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic has caused problems in many human activities. It was a sign of a sharp reduction in air traffic, and this reduction in traffic also led to a major outage of specific data used in numerical weather forecasts (NWP). This paper seeks to provide this data to the general public, based on information from the World Meteorological Organization (WMO) and other professional sources, and to show its importance in aviation, as well as how meteorologists have coped with this unusual situation.

articleTitle: Evaluation of the impacts of production facility objects construction on the operation of secondary radar
abstract: The present paper focuses on assessing the impact of production and operations objects construction on the operation of secondary radar, which is being employed in air-traffic control. We will evaluate the influence of such objects on the secondary radar parameters and its ability to detect air targets. In order to evaluate the impacts of production and operations objects construction on the secondary radar operation we will apply the methods of modelling and simulation.

articleTitle: Design of a Model of an Additional Meteorological Network for the Needs of the Aviation Component of the Integrated Rescue System
abstract: This article deals with the design of a model of an additional meteorological network, which would be a source of objective meteorological information through the innovative automatic meteorological station IMS4 Remote Observer. The current state of weather monitoring in Slovakia is insufficient for the IRS aviation component and a large part of the territory remains without meteorological monitoring. Rescue helicopter pilots do not have the opportunity to perform optimal planning of the rescue mission in the event of inappropriate or dangerous weather for the flight. The authors of the article analyze the current state, identify its shortcomings and propose a suitable type of meteorological network following the recommendations of the World Meteorological Organization based on the purpose for which the supplementary network is proposed. Subsequently, the article presents the sequence of modeling of the supplementary network, the method, and the principles of selecting suitable locations for the establishment of measuring points of the information network. The modeling procedure is logically justifiable based on the needs and procedures of flying in General Aviation conditions to which the IRS air component belongs. The article also lists the benefits that the expansion of areas with weather monitoring brings in modern times

articleTitle: Modernisation of quadcopter – case study
abstract: The article deals with the modernization of the school drone. The modernization of the UAV consisted mainly in changing the design concept and the use of 3D printing technology in the production of some parts. The aim was to modify the non-functional unmanned vehicle so that it would be operational again with minimal financial costs. At the same time, an effort was made to present the possibilities of using modern 3D printing technologies in the conditions of unmanned aerial vehicles.

articleTitle: Airport medical screening – a way to restore confidence
abstract: The aerospace industry must increase air transport resistance against health threats and regain passenger confidence. The basis of the presented secure zones concept is to create “free infectious zones” in the building terminal through airport health screening of passengers, crews, and airport workers. The concept analyses methods of detecting infectious diseases in force at the airport so that they can be available in a short time frame at an affordable cost and to the extent necessary. The potential place of the passenger health screening must be based on non-touch devices using suitable industrial standards for the regulations creation, including the implementation phase.

articleTitle: Testing Pilots' Responses on Flight Simulators - Current Status
abstract: This article presents more than 9 years of research in the field of testing pilots' responses to external stimuli - a step change in flight data – namely in flight altitude. Five simulators were used all together for long-term testing, however, statistically significant are the tests from three simulators that remain available for further testing. A simulator built on the XPlane-10 platform is the basis of most of the tests and pilots (students of University of Defence in Brno) were tested on it regularly over a 7-year period. This article presents statistics based on 37,000 analyses from all the available simulators, from all the known pilot behavior models, and also from averaged 10 step changes in flight altitude for each performed mission.

articleTitle: Changes in the Civil Aviation Legislation and Measures caused by the COVID-19 Crisis
abstract: The year 2019 is possible to consider as an extraordinary in the history of mankind. The sudden outbreak of Covid-19 virus in China has had a significant impact on daily life. The situation worsened over the weeks, so much so that a global pandemic broke out, and it was accompanied by a slowdown in the world economy. From another point of view, the pandemic caused a reduction in incomes in families, a deepening of poverty, mental problems of people, high unemployment, inflation, or interruption of the educational process in schools. Closed borders and strict rules have caused that all kinds of traffic suffered. The difficult situation was perceived by air transport, where the decline in passengers caused the bankruptcy of airlines, the grounding of aircraft and the overall decline of the sector. This paper is focused on the impact of the Covid-19 pandemic on civil aviation and the measures put in place to mitigate the spread of the Covid-19 virus. The article briefly assesses previous crises that have affected civil aviation. Then it describes the measures and changes that had to be applied in air transport to mitigate the impact of the corona crisis. From a legal point of view, it analyses the legislative solutions that were suggested by the European Union, and It evaluates the approach of the Slovak government to rescuing airports.

articleTitle: Conceptual Design of the Power Supply for the Mobile Monitoring Unit
abstract: Nowadays, various surveillance and security systems are used to detect undesirable violation of the monitored area. The physical principles of information’s gathering, methodology of their processing and subsequent evaluation are the main differences in the operational methods of surveillance and security systems, which allow a wide range of their use in applications with a large variability of potential intruders. Assuming that the surveillance and security systems are used in specific applications where the position and the total number of used individual sensing elements within the monitoring area can change over time, it is necessary, mainly due to the practical and economic reasons, to reduce their dependence on the external galvanic power connections to increase the mobility of system. The technical implementation of a power supply that is independent on the external galvanic connection can be generally in the case of complex surveillance and safety systems considered as an issue with a specific approach of solution, because their individual functional modules may require mutually different power requirements to achieve the proper system operation. In consequence, this article is devoted to the conceptual design of a power supply for a mobile monitoring system, intended to prevent human entry into a defined area to restrain the spread of viral diseases in the groups of the population. In this case, the energy independence of the system is ensured by a suitable configuration of accumulator cells designed to meet the power requirements of the monitoring unit. An additional source of energy is a photovoltaic panel, which, depending on a solar activity, recharges the accumulator cells, and therefore prolong the energy autonomy of the monitoring system. The power supply is also supplemented by a protection circuit extending the accumulators lifetime and power-tracking circuit that increases the efficiency of the photovoltaic panel. The relevant parameters of all considered components of the proposed power supply are summarized in this article, including the analysis of solar irradiance captured by the intended photovoltaic panel during the specific month of the year in a given geographic location.
